meta.document: Profile Card App — Structured Design Brief
meta.changelog: v2.0: Added brand_identity, navigation_architecture, delivery_checklist, resolved_numbers, and user_flows sections to prevent misalignment between brief and design delivery.
meta.purpose: Actionable brief for UI/visual designers covering all 16 screens (ordered by design complexity), badge iconography, typography, density, acceptance criteria, and voice/tone samples.
all_screens_by_complexity: S-02 My Card Owner View (density 3) — hero

brand_identity.purpose: LOCKED. The designer must use these names exactly as specified. Do not introduce alternative product names, codenames, or working titles in any UI mockup without written approval from the product owner.
prohibited_names: Do NOT use: Aura, Aura Identity, Curator, CardMe, TG Card, or any other invented name in UI chrome, splash screens, settings footers, or marketing copy.
brand_identity.footer_text: Profile Card v{version} — Built on Telegram
brand_identity.tone_of_footer: Functional and neutral. Do NOT use aspirational or exclusionary language like 'Built for the elite' or 'For power users only.' The product is for all Telegram users.
brand_identity.domain: yourcard.link (pending OQ-7 resolution — use this as placeholder in all mockups)

navigation_architecture.purpose: Canonical navigation model. The designer must implement exactly this structure. Do not create alternative tab bars, rename tabs, or reassign screens to different tabs without written approval.

tab_bar.position: Bottom of screen, always visible on primary screens

header_actions.position: Top-right of screen on S-02 (My Card)

modal_sheets: S-06 Badge Detail (bottom sheet from any badge tap)
S-08 Share Sheet (bottom sheet from Share action)
full_screen_overlays: S-14 Badge Earned Celebration (triggered by badge unlock)
S-13 Platform Connect (triggered from S-09 or S-05 locked badge)
standalone_flows: S-10 Story Editor (from S-02 story banner tap)
S-16 Web Card Page (external browser, not in-app)

contextual_navigation.S-04_viewer_view: Opened when tapping another user's card from S-11 Feed, notifications, or direct link
contextual_navigation.S-12_analytics: Accessed from S-02 action bar or S-09 settings

tab_bar_visibility_rules: Tab bar is visible on: S-02, S-05, S-07, S-09, S-11, S-12, S-15
Tab bar is hidden on: S-01, S-03, S-04, S-06, S-08, S-10, S-13, S-14, S-16
Hidden screens use a back/close button in the top-left to return to the previous screen

user_flows.purpose: Core user journeys that show how screens connect. The designer must ensure every screen in a flow has been delivered and that transitions between screens are accounted for in the mockups.

flow_1_first_time_user.name: First Launch → Card Created
steps: App opens → S-01 Onboarding (Step 1: avatar + name auto-pulled from Telegram)
S-01 Step 2: Choose base card theme (3 free options)
S-01 Step 3: Card assembles with materialisation animation
S-01 Step 4: 'Your card is live' → CTA: 'Explore Your Card'
→ S-02 My Card (Owner View) — tab bar now visible

flow_2_share_loop.name: Owner Shares Card → Viewer Opens → Converts
steps: S-02 My Card → tap Share in action bar
→ S-08 Share Sheet (bottom sheet): choose Image or Link
Image path: PNG sent in Telegram chat → recipient sees card thumbnail
Link path: yourcard.link/@username shared → recipient opens in browser
→ S-16 Web Card Page (if link) or inline preview (if image)
→ S-04 Viewer View (if opened in Telegram Mini App)
→ Viewer taps 'Build your own card' CTA → S-01 Onboarding (new user)
flow_2_share_loop.note: This is the primary growth loop. Every screen in this flow is required.

flow_3_platform_connect.name: Connect Platform → Earn Badges → Celebrate
steps: S-09 Settings → Connected Platforms → tap 'Connect GitHub'
→ S-13 Platform Connect (OAuth consent screen)
→ External OAuth redirect → return to app
→ S-13 progress indicator ('Checking your badges on GitHub...')
→ S-14 Badge Earned Celebration (sequential carousel if multiple badges)
→ S-02 My Card (badges now visible in collection)

flow_4_badge_shop_purchase.name: Browse Shop → Preview → Purchase → Equip
steps: Tab bar → S-07 Badge Shop
Browse featured carousel or category grid → tap item
→ Live preview overlay (shows badge/theme on user's actual card)
→ Tap 'Buy' → Telegram Stars native payment
→ Confirmation animation (ka-ching + sparkle)
→ Badge appears in S-05 Badge Collection
→ User can tap badge → S-06 Badge Detail → 'Pin to Card'
→ S-02 My Card (badge now pinned)

flow_5_card_customisation.name: Edit Card Appearance
steps: S-02 My Card → tap Edit in action bar
→ S-03 Card Editor (live preview top, tabs bottom)
Browse Theme / Badges / Widgets / Frame tabs
Tap items → live preview updates instantly
Tap 'Save' → PNG re-rendered → CDN cache busted
→ S-02 My Card (updated card visible)

flow_6_discovery_and_aspiration.name: Browse Feed → View Card → Get Inspired
steps: Tab bar → S-11 Discovery Feed
Browse Trending / Top Badges / New & Notable / Staff Picks
Tap a card thumbnail → S-04 Viewer View
Tap a badge → S-06 Badge Detail (bottom sheet)
See 'View All Badges' → S-05 Badge Collection (public variant, no locked section)
Get inspired → return to S-02 → tap Edit → S-03 Card Editor

S-01_onboarding.title: Onboarding / Card Creation
S-01_onboarding.prd_purpose: First-time user creates their card in under 60 seconds.

visual_references.what_to_borrow: Card-as-metaphor anatomy: logo/avatar strip at top, hero identity zone in the middle, badge/stat strip below, shareable barcode/QR at the bottom. Layered elevation via light overlays and subtle borders. The card 'materialises' on screen rather than appearing statically.
specific_elements: Rounded corners with subtle shadow for depth
Consistent card anatomy across all card types
Dark mode palette #1C1C1E with #E0E0E0 text

visual_references.what_to_borrow: All chrome colours inherited from themeParams. Day/Night switching must work automatically. Use TelegramUI React components for the input step (name, avatar selection).
specific_elements: bg_color and secondary_bg_color as the base layer
button_color for the primary CTA
Real-time theme sync on toggle

visual_references.what_to_borrow: One-stat-per-step simplicity. Each onboarding step should present a single action or choice — never two decisions on one screen. Black-and-white base with a single vivid accent keeps each step fresh.
specific_elements: Single focal point per step
Bold sans-serif display text for the headline
Scratchy analog texture accents for warmth

anti_references.what_to_avoid: Multi-field forms crammed onto one screen. Completeness progress bars that create anxiety rather than excitement. Corporate blue sterility.
anti_references.reason: Onboarding must feel like 30 seconds of play, not 5 minutes of form-filling.

anti_references.what_to_avoid: Overwhelming grid of customisation options presented before the user has context for why they matter. Feature overload on first touch.
anti_references.reason: The editor is S-03. Onboarding (S-01) is about instant card creation with Telegram data — defer customisation.

emotional_target.user_inner_monologue: This is going to be cool AND I can do it in 30 seconds.
emotional_target.anxiety_level: Near zero — every step has one obvious action
emotional_target.anticipation_level: High — the card preview builds progressively as they step through
emotional_target.animation_mood: Playful entrance animations; the card materialises from sparks/particles as it assembles step by step
emotional_target.sound: Subtle chime on card creation complete

density.rationale: Spotify Wrapped one-stat-per-card approach. Maximum whitespace. Zero cognitive overload.

S-01_onboarding.layout_guidance: 3–4 full-screen steps: (1) Telegram avatar + name auto-pulled with a 'This is you' confirmation, (2) choose a base card theme (3 free options), (3) card assembles with animation, (4) 'Your card is ready — share or explore.' Each step is a swipeable page, not a scroll.

S-02_my_card_owner_view.title: My Card (Owner View)
S-02_my_card_owner_view.prd_purpose: The user's own card as they see it. Hub for all actions. Shows pinned badges (5 free / 8 premium), live widgets, story banner, and action bar.

visual_references.what_to_borrow: Modular showcase blocks on a dark canvas. Level-gated unlocks that pace content density. Self-reinforcing badge → level → showcase slot flywheel. Dark background (#1B2838) makes colourful badges pop.
specific_elements: Modular blocks the user can reorder
Progression-gated slots (free → premium)
High-contrast colourful elements on dark base

visual_references.what_to_borrow: One hero metric as the emotional anchor (streak flame = total badge score or card views). Colour-coded badge progression tiers (grey → bronze → silver → gold). Celebration animations drive screenshot-sharing.
specific_elements: Large, bold hero number front and centre
Colour tiers for rarity without labels
Badge unlock drives store purchases (+13%) and friend-adds (+116%)

visual_references.what_to_borrow: Asymmetric bento-grid layout with mixed content types (text, image, embed, stat, link). Each tile independently styled. Glassmorphism overlays for depth on gradient backgrounds.
specific_elements: Variable-size widget tiles
Frosted-glass overlay on card surface
Each tile independently shareable

visual_references.what_to_borrow: Contribution heatmap as un-fakeable activity proof. Shields.io-style pill badges for compact metadata. Streak counter mechanic. Pinned repos = curated best work showcase.
specific_elements: Activity heatmap widget possibility
Pill-style stat indicators
Pinned slots = curated showcase

anti_references.what_to_avoid: Uniform square grid with no hierarchy. Every tile the same size communicates nothing about priority. Content-heavy but meaning-light.
anti_references.reason: The owner view needs visual hierarchy: hero metric > pinned badges > widgets > story. Not a flat grid of equal items.

anti_references.what_to_avoid: NFT-centric aesthetic (hexagonal frames, blockchain terminology, wallet-connect UX). Crypto-native visual language alienates 95% of Telegram users.
anti_references.reason: Profile Card is cosmetic-first, not crypto-first. Stars economy, not wallet economy.

emotional_target.user_inner_monologue: This is MY identity card. It looks incredible and it's all real.
emotional_target.pride_source: Earned badges with ✓ checkmarks prove real achievement
emotional_target.ownership_signal: Customised theme, curated pinned badges, personal story banner
emotional_target.animation_mood: Subtle breathing/shimmer on the card surface; badges gently pulse on first view of the day
emotional_target.sound: None — this is the ambient home screen

density.max_elements: 8–12 visual elements in a structured bento grid
density.breakdown: Avatar + username + story banner + pinned badges (5–8) + 1–2 live stat widgets + action bar (edit, share, settings)
density.rationale: Bento-grid medium density. Enough to feel 'full' and impressive without overwhelming.

S-02_my_card_owner_view.layout_guidance: Apple Wallet card anatomy: avatar strip at top → hero identity zone (name, level, hero metric) → pinned badge row (horizontal scroll or 2-row grid) → live widget tiles (bento layout) → story banner → action bar (edit, share, analytics). Card viewport uses purchasable theme overlay; app chrome uses Telegram themeParams.

S-05_badge_collection.title: Badge Collection
S-05_badge_collection.prd_purpose: Full badge inventory. Owner variant shows earned (by platform, rarity-sorted), purchased (by pack/date), special (trophies section), and locked (greyed, criteria visible). Public viewer variant omits locked badges.

visual_references.what_to_borrow: Dense mosaic grid where the sheer count IS the status signal. Trophy-tier colour system (bronze/silver/gold/platinum) with zero learning curve. Dynamic rarity display based on global earn rate.
specific_elements: Dense icon grid — visual density = dedication signal
Tier colours universally understood
Fractional XP from partial progress keeps engagement

visual_references.what_to_borrow: Colour-coded progression (grey → bronze → silver → gold) makes rarity instantly readable. Scrollable achievement sections with clear groupings.
specific_elements: Rarity readable at a glance via colour
Section grouping by category/platform
Locked badges with visible unlock criteria

visual_references.what_to_borrow: Heatmap-density visual for earned authenticity. Shields.io pill badges for metadata. The collection should feel like a living portfolio, not a static list.
specific_elements: Platform-grouped sections with headers
Earned authenticity principle front and centre
Streak counter for engagement

anti_references.what_to_avoid: Flat text lists with no visual differentiation. Badges rendered as text titles in a table. No colour, no iconography, no density.
anti_references.reason: The collection must be visual-first. The grid of icons IS the experience — not a data table.

anti_references.platform: App Store Badge Walls (e.g., Foursquare legacy)
anti_references.what_to_avoid: All badges same size, same border, same prominence. No rarity signal. Every badge feels equally worthless when displayed identically.
anti_references.reason: Rarity rings, glow effects, and locked-state visual differentiation are non-negotiable.

emotional_target.user_inner_monologue_earned: Look at everything I've built. This is my story.
emotional_target.user_inner_monologue_locked: I'm 2 commits away from that badge. Let me go earn it.
emotional_target.satisfaction_driver: Seeing a dense, colourful grid of earned badges with ✓ checkmarks
emotional_target.aspiration_driver: Greyed-out locked badges with visible criteria create pull
emotional_target.animation_mood: Earned badges glow softly on their rarity colour; locked badges have a subtle 'unlock' shimmer on tap
emotional_target.sound: None — this is a browsing/inventory screen

density.max_elements: 150+ badge icons in a dense scrollable grid
density.grid_spec: 4–5 columns on mobile at 32dp icon size, expanding to 6–8 on tablet/web
density.section_structure: Special (Trophies) → Earned (grouped by platform, rarity desc) → Purchased (by pack/date) → Locked (criteria visible)
density.rationale: PlayStation mosaic density. The visual mass of badges IS the status signal. Dense and proud.

S-05_badge_collection.layout_guidance: Sticky top bar with badge count summary (e.g., '47 / 150 earned'). Section headers with platform icons. Each badge is a 32dp rounded-square with rarity-coloured ring. Tap opens S-06 badge detail sheet. Owner view: locked badges at bottom with greyed state + unlock criteria tooltip. Viewer view: no locked section.

badge_icon_style_direction.system: Dual-layer icon system — badge icons are illustrative, UI icons are outlined

badge_icons.style: Filled, rounded, illustrative — each badge tells a micro-story through its icon
badge_icons.shape: Rounded square with 8dp corner radius, matching Telegram's sticker/emoji shape language

rarity_ring.width: 2dp solid ring around the badge icon

effects.uncommon: Solid ring + subtle green flash on unlock
effects.rare: Solid ring + shimmer overlay that moves across the surface
effects.epic: Solid ring + soft outer glow (4dp blur, rarity colour at 30% opacity)
effects.legendary: Solid ring + particle burst aura + golden shimmer

class_indicators.earned: ✓ checkmark inset at bottom-right, 12dp, white icon on rarity-colour circle
class_indicators.purchased: ⭐ star inset at bottom-right, 12dp, white icon on #FF375F (Stars Pink) circle
class_indicators.special: ☆ outline star inset at bottom-right, 12dp, #FFD700 (Star Gold) on dark circle

badge_icons.platform_source: 8dp monochrome platform logo watermark at top-left corner of badge icon

locked_state.border: Dotted line replacing solid rarity ring
locked_state.overlay: Subtle lock icon at centre (optional, only in collection grid)

illustration_principles: Each badge icon should be recognisable at 32dp — avoid fine detail that disappears at small sizes
Use the platform's brand colour as a dominant fill (e.g., GitHub badges lean dark/green, Spotify badges lean green/black)
Achievement icons should depict the accomplishment metaphorically (e.g., 'Star Collector' = star constellation, not a literal number)
Avoid photographic or hyper-realistic styles — keep to flat/semi-flat illustrative with subtle gradients
Maintain a consistent 2dp internal padding from the icon edge to the rarity ring
design_system_references: Shields.io pill format for metadata indicators

ui_icons.style: Outlined, 2dp stroke, rounded caps and joins — matching Telegram's native icon language
ui_icons.colour_inheritance: hint_color for secondary, text_color for primary, button_color for interactive — all from Telegram themeParams

platform_connection_icons.style: Monochrome brand logos at 20dp; full-colour on connected state
platform_connection_icons.source: Simple Icons (2400+ brand SVGs) or official platform brand kits

typography.font_stack: System default — SF Pro (iOS), Roboto (Android) — inherited from Telegram for native feel

hero_display.use: Celebration badge name, hero metric on S-02, onboarding headlines

section_heading.use: Section headers in badge collection, shop categories, settings groups

badge_label.use: Badge name under icon in collection grid

stat_number.use: Analytics counters, card view count, Stars balance
stat_number.style: Tabular lining figures, monospaced digits for alignment

principles: Hero stats use Spotify Wrapped-style bold sans-serif display — large, confident, single-number storytelling
All other text uses Telegram's native typography system for seamless integration
Numbers always use tabular (monospaced) lining figures so counters don't shift layout during animation
Maximum two font weights per screen to avoid visual noise

level_definitions.1_sparse: Single focal point per viewport. ≥60% whitespace. One action.
level_definitions.2_focused: 2–5 elements with clear hierarchy. ~50% whitespace. Informational.
level_definitions.3_balanced: 8–12 elements in structured layout. ~40% whitespace. Scannable hub.
level_definitions.4_rich: Mixed zones — spacious hero section + dense browsable grid. ~30% whitespace.
level_definitions.5_packed: Maximum visual density. Scrollable grids of 20+ items. The density IS the point.

global.criterion: Every screen renders correctly in both Telegram Day and Night themes, inheriting all colours from themeParams in real-time — no hardcoded colour values in app chrome.
Card viewport uses purchasable theme overlays; app chrome ALWAYS uses Telegram themeParams. These two layers are visually distinct.
All animations run at 60fps on a mid-range Android device (e.g., Samsung Galaxy A34). Use Lottie/Rive, not CSS-only animations for complex sequences.
Badge icons are legible and their rarity colour ring is distinguishable at 32dp (smallest collection grid size).
✓ (earned), ⭐ (purchased), and ☆ (special) class indicators are visually distinct at 12dp inset size.
Share artefacts (PNG export) are legible at 280×280px chat-bubble thumbnail size — one stat, one emotion, one accent colour per card.
No screen exceeds its assigned density level. Density violations require design review.
All numbers use tabular lining figures so counters do not shift layout during count-up animations.

S-01_onboarding.criterion: Card creation completes in ≤4 taps and ≤60 seconds from app open.
Each onboarding step displays exactly one input/action — never two decisions on one screen.
The card preview builds progressively across steps, with each step adding a visible element.
Final step plays a card-materialisation animation (sparks/particles) lasting 1–2 seconds.
Avatar and name are auto-populated from the Telegram profile with no manual input required.

S-02_my_card.criterion: Card layout follows Apple Wallet anatomy: avatar strip → hero zone → badge row → widget tiles → story → action bar.
One hero metric (badge score, card views, or level) is displayed at 28–36sp bold as the emotional anchor.
Pinned badge row shows 5 badges (free) or 8 badges (premium) with horizontal scroll if needed.
Earned badges display ✓ checkmark; purchased show ⭐; special show ☆. These are visible at card level, not only on tap.
Card surface has a subtle breathing/shimmer animation that responds to the active theme.
Story banner is visible at the top of the card when active, with text legible at 14sp.

S-05_badge_collection.criterion: Badge grid displays at 4–5 columns on mobile (32dp per icon) with rarity ring visible on every badge.
Sections follow the order: Special (Trophies) → Earned (by platform, rarity desc) → Purchased (by pack/date) → Locked (criteria visible). Owner view only for locked section.
Locked badges render in greyscale at 40% opacity with dotted border. Tap reveals unlock criteria.
Sticky top bar shows progress summary (e.g., '47 / 150 earned') and remains visible during scroll.
Tapping any earned/purchased badge opens the S-06 Badge Detail sheet within 200ms.
Public viewer variant omits the 'Locked' section entirely.

principles.brand_personality: Confident but warm. Playful but not childish. Achievement-focused but not elitist. The voice of a friend who's genuinely hyped about your accomplishments.
principles.formality_level: Casual-professional. Think Discord system messages meets Duolingo encouragement. Never corporate, never slangy.
principles.verified_not_self_declared: Every reference to badges or stats should subtly reinforce that these are EARNED and REAL — not self-reported.

base_palette.note: Fallbacks only. Production reads from Telegram themeParams.

design_principles_checklist: Dark-first, light-compatible: design for Night mode as primary, adapt to Day mode via themeParams.
Card-as-metaphor: every profile card follows Apple Wallet anatomy (avatar strip → hero zone → badge row → share action).
Earned authenticity: visual hierarchy always privileges earned/verified content over purchased cosmetics.
Bento modularity: the card and web view are composed of independently-styled widget tiles.
Chat-bubble-optimised: share artefacts must be legible at 280×280px thumbnail.
Proportional celebration: animation intensity scales with badge rarity.
Theme-aware particles: celebration effects use card theme accent colours, not hardcoded values.
Progressive reveal: multi-badge unlock uses sequential carousel with micro-narrative tension.
One-tap share: from 'see data' to 'broadcast identity' in a single gesture.
